set.v: Share of a robbery haul; the 1903 wire says about $40,000 in gold coin and diamonds in two satchels

tw-mi-grand-haven-light-house-hill-convi.st: A 1903 wire gave the fullest version: the dying Jackson convict told Gray (called the county sheriff there; he was coroner) that loot from 'a sensational robbery in Kalamazoo', about $40,000 in gold coin and diamonds in two satchels, had been carried up the shore from Saugatuck by two crooks and buried near Five-Mile Hill, 'in the lake shore sands within the city limits of Grand Haven'. Gray searched without success, then told friends, and parties hunted 'year after year'.
tw-mi-grand-haven-light-house-hill-convi.t: The sums grow with each retelling: several thousand dollars in 1899, gold and diamonds in 1900, $40,000 in 1903.
src: Detroit News, 15 Oct 1903, p. 3, 'Buried Treasure / Grand Haven People Have Long Searched For It' (Newspapers.com 1377937784); same wire Battle Creek Enquirer, 17 Oct 1903, p. 3
